When does the flow's posterior stop depending on the integrator?

Each of the eval's 10 injections is sampled from one trained flow with the ODE integrator varied: 4 to 256 steps, three step schedules and two update rules. A converged sampler gives per-source widths that no longer move as steps grow; a sampler that collapses gives widths that keep growing. Cost per call is in sampling cost.

Does the score keep improving with more network calls?

Median over sources of the CRPS at the truth, as a ratio to the reference cell, against network calls per draw (midpoint: two a step, Euler: one, plus the first). Below 1 the cell scores better than the reference: with one injection per source that is noise unless it holds across schedules.
